title: Molecular Dynamics Study on Wear Resistance of High Entropy Alloy Coatings Considering the Effect of Temperature

recollection.starting_material: Model high-entropy alloy coating, probably an equiatomic FCC solid solution such as CoCrFeNi (sometimes with Mo or Mn) represented by a large atomistic slab on a rigid substrate
recollection.intervention: Classical molecular-dynamics scratch/slide simulations in which a rigid diamond or spherical indenter is pressed and slid across the coating at various temperatures (e.g., 300 K, 600 K, 900 K)
recollection.structure: Initial single-phase FCC solid solution; during sliding the near-surface region develops a highly defected nanocrystalline or amorphous layer whose thickness depends on temperature
recollection.mechanism: Wear proceeds by dislocation nucleation and motion, local amorphization and atomic mixing; increasing temperature enhances atomic diffusion, accelerates dislocation recovery, and reduces the pile-up height, thereby lowering friction but increasing material removal
recollection.results: Simulated wear depth grows from ~2–3 nm after a fixed sliding distance at 300 K to ~5–6 nm at 900 K; friction coefficient drops from about 0.30 to 0.15 over the same temperature range; hardness extracted from indentation curves decreases by ~25 % with every 300 K rise in temperature; the HEA coating still outperforms a pure Ni reference by ~30 % lower wear volume under all conditions

score.note: The recollection broadly identifies temperature-dependent MD indentation/sliding and an FCC coating with defect accumulation, but it misidentifies the FeNiCrCoCu/Cu system and omits key simulation parameters. Its proposed mechanism conflicts with the paper: above 900 K, lattice disorder and softening increase tangential force and friction rather than lowering friction. The numerical wear depths, friction coefficients, hardness trend, and Ni comparison are unsupported or incorrect.
